result:
Repo is clean — only the deliverable files were added:

- **`target_app.py`** — the FastAPI app exposed as `app`, at the repo root.
- **`bulletin_project/serving_settings.py`** — `from bulletin_project.settings import *` (reuses the unchanged `BENCH_DB_PATH` DB wiring) then strips every `rest_framework*` entry from `INSTALLED_APPS`.
- **`posts/serving_models.py`** — an unmanaged Django model shadowing `authtoken_token` so the serving process can validate tokens via the ORM without `rest_framework.authtoken` in `INSTALLED_APPS` (and thus without ever importing `rest_framework`).

No existing files were modified or deleted.

Verification performed (then removed, since it was scratch tooling): seeded an identical SQLite DB via the original Django/DRF app, ran all 13 scenarios from `public-tests/scenarios.json` through the real Django test client, then in a **separate fresh process that only ever imports `target_app`** ran the same scenarios through FastAPI's `TestClient`. Results:

- All 13 scenarios matched exactly — status codes, JSON bodies (including exact DRF error strings like `"Invalid token header. No credentials provided."`), and the `allow`/`www-authenticate` headers.
- Resulting SQLite rows in `posts_post` were byte-identical between the two runs after the full scenario sequence (post 1 deleted, post 3 created, post 2 unchanged).
- Confirmed `rest_framework`, `django.core.asgi`, `django.core.wsgi`, `django.core.handlers`, and `django.test` never appear in `sys.modules` after importing `target_app`.
- Confirmed `django.conf.settings.INSTALLED_APPS` in the serving process has no `rest_framework*` entries.

Key behaviors replicated natively (no DRF): `TokenAuthentication`'s exact error strings for missing/malformed/invalid tokens, `IsAuthenticated`/`IsAuthorOrReadOnly` permission ordering (401 before 403, 404 before permission check), DRF's per-route `Allow` header (set on every response for that route regardless of status, mirroring `APIView.dispatch`), and `PostSerializer` field validation (blank/required/max-length messages, read-only `id`/`author`).
